author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Roadside assistance is a service that may arrange help when a vehicle cannot continue its journey, under the terms of the actual contract. Do not assume that every motor policy includes a roadside repair, towing, passenger transport or a replacement vehicle. For a driver in Moldova, useful preparation starts with the vehicle, route and procedure for requesting help, rather than a promise of “help anywhere”.

This article provides questions for comparing services. It does not confirm that ING Broker sells a particular assistance package. Availability and conditions require individual confirmation. It gives no repair instructions or directions for working in a dangerous location. If people are at risk, follow the competent authorities and obtain appropriate help. Safety must remain separate from a commercial discussion about who pays.

Roadside assistance, RCA and CASCO serve different purposes

A third-party motor liability policy and a policy for your own vehicle do not, by themselves, explain who sends a recovery truck. Read each policy and service document, then ask which interventions are provided. A telephone number printed on a policy may be for reporting claims, not for coordinating breakdown assistance. Do not assume that the same contact approves every expense.

Separate arranging help from paying for it. Finding an available provider is one question; paying the invoice within stated limits is another. Ask for an answer under the contract being considered. An insurer's public description of an additional service does not prove that it is included in your existing policy or that every operation involves no payment by you.

Which reasons for being unable to continue should you discuss?

Prepare separate questions about breakdowns, accidents, a flat battery, a damaged tyre and any other issue relevant to your vehicle. These examples are not a guaranteed list of services. Ask how an accepted situation is defined and whether the document contains additional conditions. A voluntary stop and a technical problem should not be treated as identical without checking.

Explain whether the vehicle was already defective when assistance was requested. Do not assume that a new contract resolves a known immobilisation. Describe a recurring problem accurately. Understanding the limits before departure is more useful than seeking retrospective confirmation after the car can no longer move. Keep any unresolved question visible rather than selecting the answer you hope applies.

The vehicle must match the service conditions

Provide the vehicle category, weight and use, along with the information requested by the provider. Ask explicitly about a commercial vehicle, caravan, trailer or special-purpose vehicle. An answer for an ordinary passenger car does not confirm eligibility for another category. For a fleet, the service needs to be related to each vehicle actually included, not just the company's name.

Ask whether vehicle age, condition or use matters where the documents contain such conditions. This article sets no universal age limit and confirms no category accepted by every provider. When replacing the car, check how the contract is updated. A subscription or policy for one registration number should not be assumed to follow every vehicle driven by the same person.

Check the territory against the whole route

Record the destination and transit countries, then ask for confirmation of the service territory. Do not infer assistance conditions from Green Card or CASCO territory. If two routes are possible, explain both. Check the contract period against the return journey as well as departure. An old quotation may describe different conditions from the document currently offered.

Ask about assistance in difficult-to-reach areas and restrictions where providers cannot work. The word “abroad” is not a universal promise. Seek an answer before travelling if the situation is unclear. Road safety and access are separate matters. An assistance contract does not guarantee that every route is passable or that a provider can reach every location.

How do you request help, and who authorises it?

Save the official number for requesting assistance and learn what information is needed during the call. Relevant details may include the contract identifier, vehicle and location needed to deliver the service. Use the official channel. Do not publish an exact position or vehicle documents in an open group hoping that somebody else will activate the service for you.

Ask about authorisation and what happens if you have already ordered a recovery truck yourself. A contract does not automatically reimburse any invoice. Keep the request reference and relevant communications without unnecessarily recording or distributing other people's details. If an instruction is unclear, seek confirmation before accepting a cost that may remain your responsibility.

Towing: destination and limits matter

Ask where the vehicle may be taken: a nearby workshop, an appointed provider or another destination specified in the contract. Check how distance is measured and whether expense limits apply. This article gives no universal kilometre allowance. Two services described as “towing” may differ substantially in their permitted collection point, destination and authorisation arrangements.

Separate moving the vehicle from repairing it. Recovery does not confirm spare-part availability, the repair price or when the car will be ready. For a company vehicle, notify the person responsible for its use and the property inside. Do not assume that the same intervention includes handling or insurance for cargo or valuable equipment carried in the car.

Passengers and continuing the journey

If passenger transport, accommodation or a replacement vehicle matters, ask about each separately. Check the eligible people, situations and limits. A feature mentioned in advertising is not a promise that every family member's or colleague's expenses will be paid. Request the document confirming the service available for your circumstances rather than relying on a general benefit description.

Explain any fixed schedule or related reservations. Roadside assistance should not be assumed equivalent to cancellation insurance or reimbursement for a missed meeting. Check the contractual basis and required evidence for each expense. Retain relevant reservations and invoices, but do not collect passenger information before understanding what is needed and who should receive it.

Which expenses may remain with the owner?

Ask about parts, fuel, labour, storage, additional orders and other costs important to you. These categories are not declared included or excluded here. The purpose is to understand the offer before using it. A deductible, where applicable, is the part of a cost or loss retained under the contract. It is not the premium paid for insurance.

Ask about the number of permitted interventions, waiting periods or other restrictions where stated in the documents. Do not compare the annual price alone. Request written clarification of unclear costs. No answer does not establish that a service is free. A suitable option has limits you understand, rather than merely the most impressive advertising language.

Example: the car will not start before the return journey

A driver finds that the car will not start in the parking area where it was left. They first consider whether safety assistance is required, then use the contact in the assistance contract. This is an illustrative example, not a customer case. It provides no technical diagnosis and confirms neither acceptance of the fault nor dispatch of a particular response.

The driver supplies relevant details, asks what is being arranged and which costs require authorisation, then retains the request confirmation. They do not order several providers assuming every bill will be reimbursed. If the car goes to a workshop, repairs are discussed separately. The record distinguishes the requested service, confirmed response and unresolved expenses without promises made on the provider's behalf.

Pre-contract checking sheet

  • The vehicle, category and use are described accurately.
  • The territory and period match the whole journey.
  • Accepted reasons for immobilisation are explained in the documents.
  • The official assistance number and contract identification procedure are available.
  • Provider authorisation, towing destination and relevant limits are understood.
  • Parts, repairs and additional services are clarified separately.
  • Any passenger services are confirmed rather than assumed.
  • The records needed for a reimbursement request are identified.

What should you record before accepting a package?

A simple comparison can use separate rows for towing, an on-site intervention, passenger transport and possible accommodation. For each, record who arranges it, who pays, the stated limit and the required approval. Leave unanswered fields visible. An advertising tick does not explain these differences or replace the service conditions. Keep the answer linked to the document and version actually being considered.

If other family members drive the car, check who receives the instructions and whether service access follows the person or the vehicle. The driver should be able to find the official contact and contract details without somebody else's personal password. This is preparation for accessing information, not a test call or an order for real services. It does not establish provider availability.

Frequently asked questions about roadside assistance

Does RCA mean that towing is included?

Do not assume so. Check for a separate service or an explicit provision in the documents received. Motor liability insurance and arranging an intervention are different benefits.

Can I order any recovery truck and then claim the money?

Ask about the procedure before ordering. The contract may require a particular form of authorisation and documentation. An invoice alone does not establish reimbursement.

Will the car always be repaired on the spot?

This article makes no such promise. The response depends on the actual situation, provider capabilities and service conditions. Diagnosis and operational safety belong to the appropriate specialists.

What if I cannot find the service documents?

Contact the provider through its official channel and clarify how to identify the contract. Do not send card details or passwords for a supposed activation. Make the documents accessible before the next journey.
